subject: Clarify pen-test notice and evidence cadence for Order Form
messages:
From: Tom Barnes <tom.barnes@medisage.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Clarify audit scope and pen-test notice in Order Form

Hi Karthik / Laura,

Thanks for sending the draft Order Form. Two quick asks from our security team before we can move to signature:

1) Pen-test notice window — the draft says "reasonable notice". For procurement we need a concrete minimum notice/maximum notice and whether lateral/staging access is allowed. Can Redwood confirm the required notice period and whether short-notice emergency tests are permitted?

2) Evidence cadence — we typically ask for quarterly evidence snapshots and a rolling SOC2 Type II report. Can you share the recommended cadence Redwood expects to provide (weekly logs, quarterly snapshots, ad-hoc deeper dives)?

Emily from our security group is copied — she can share any internal constraints. We appreciate flexibility but need specifics for our internal risk committee.

- Tom
Tom Barnes
Director, IT Procurement
MediSage Health

Attachments: none
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tom Barnes <tom.barnes@medisage.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 20:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Clarify audit scope and pen-test notice in Order Form

Tom / Emily — thanks for the clear callouts. Short answer: we can propose concrete language and one pragmatic compromise that keeps your security committee comfortable while preserving our operational constraints.

High-level proposal (we'll attach a redline of the MSA/order form):
- Pen-test notice: 48 hours non-invasive notice for standard vulnerability scans; for full exploit-style penetration tests we require 7 business days notice and a scoped test plan.
- Lateral/staging access: lateral access is allowed on customer-provided staging environments only; we do not grant lateral access to multi-tenant production environments.
- Emergency tests: we can accept emergency or incident-driven tests with 24-hour coordination, subject to mutual written approval and an agreed rollback plan.
- Evidence cadence: standard delivery is 
  * weekly token-level audit logs (retention summary) via secure link,
  * quarterly evidence snapshots (configuration, access lists, sample logs), and
  * an annual SOC 2 Type II report (we can provide the latest report on execution).

I'll loop Legal and Ops for the precise redline language. Laura / Marissa — can you review and add legal-friendly phrasing? I attached a short draft to this thread in a follow-up.

Thanks,
Karthik
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 14:17:00 -0500
Subject: internal: suggested language for Notice / Pen-test clauses

Karthik / Marissa — quick internal kernel before we send to MediSage:

I reviewed the draft and propose trimming the options to two concrete buckets so we don't re-open scope during procurement:

1) Non-invasive scans (automated vulnerability scanning, dependency scans): 48 hours notice; allowed on production endpoints; no lateral access. No explicit staging requirement.
2) Targeted penetration testing (active exploitation, lateral movement, account takeover attempts): 7 business days notice + a scoped test plan and named tester(s); allowed only on customer-provided staging or ephemeral testbeds; explicit prohibition on testing customer production without a separate addendum. Emergency incident-driven tests: allowed with 24-hour written approval and point-of-contact + rollback plan filed.

For evidence cadence — keep what Karthik suggested but add a bit more detail: weekly anonymized token-level logs (retention 90 days), quarterly evidence snapshot (config exports, access control lists, sample audit logs, and list of systems in scope), and SOC 2 Type II report annually. Add a clause that Redwood will provide a pen-test summary report redacted for third-party tooling if needed.

If that sounds right I will prepare clean redline language and a short XLS that maps the evidence items to delivery cadence (easy for procurement to attach to the order form).

- Laura
VP, Legal — Redwood Inference

Attachments: none

Subject: Proposed redlines and evidence cadence for Order Form (files attached)

Tom / Emily — attaching the proposed redline and a simple evidence-cadence worksheet so your review cycle is quicker.

Summary of the attached items (high level):
- MSA_redline_MediSage_20261105.pdf: Clean redline that implements the two-bucket approach Laura outlined above. Key points: 48hr notice for non-invasive scans; 7 business days + scoped plan for active pentests; lateral access limited to customer-provided staging; emergency incident-testing path with 24-hour written approval.
- SOC2-type2-summary-2026.pdf: Executive summary and date of last assessment. Full SOC2 reports can be shared under NDA; if you need the full report we can push an NDA + secure portal link.
- evidence-cadence-proposal-20261105.xlsx: Row-level mapping of deliverable -> cadence -> delivery method. Example rows: weekly token-level logs (secure S3 link), quarterly evidence snapshot (SFTP or secure Drive), annual SOC2 report (PDF via secure portal).

If that looks good, we can convert the redline into a one-paragraph exhibit to sit on the Order Form and close the loop. If Emily has any specific constraints (e.g., required retention >90 days) shout and we can evaluate.

Next steps: please review the redline and the XLS; we can set a 30-minute call if you prefer to walk through the buckets.

Best,
Karthik
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
